name: RESTful API Design Standards & Maturity
description: Designing and governing organization-wide RESTful API standards from resource modeling to hypermedia maturity. IMPORTANT DISTINCTION: Backend's be_api_design.restful_principles covers a developer implementing GET/POST/PUT endpoints in their own service with correct status codes (daily coding); API Design's api_rest_design covers establishing the organization's REST maturity model, writing the API style guide that all teams must follow, defining mandatory error response schemas (RFC 7807), and governing schema evolution compatibility rules across hundreds of APIs (strategic/architectural decision-making). The backend developer writes an endpoint; the API designer writes the standard that governs how all endpoints are written.

subskills.name: Resource Modeling & Domain Taxonomy
subskills.description: Designing canonical resource models that represent business domains — defining resource boundaries, sub-resource relationships, singleton vs collection resources, and establishing a shared resource taxonomy across API teams.

subskills.name: HATEOAS & Richardson Maturity Model
subskills.description: Evaluating and selecting the appropriate Richardson Maturity Level (0-3) for organizational APIs, designing HATEOAS link relations (RFC 8288), and governing hypermedia-driven API navigation standards.

subskills.name: Collection Pagination & Filtering Standards
subskills.description: Defining platform-wide pagination conventions — cursor-based vs offset pagination mandates, standardized page metadata envelope shapes, filtering parameter syntax (field[operator]=value), and sorting conventions across all collection endpoints.

subskills.name: Error Response Standards (RFC 7807/9457)
subskills.description: Designing and enforcing organization-wide error response schemas based on RFC 7807/9457 Problem Details — mandatory fields, custom extension fields, error type URI taxonomy, and localized error message strategies.

subskills.name: Query Language & Filtering Specifications
subskills.description: Selecting and standardizing API query languages — OData $filter syntax, JSON:API sparse fieldsets, GraphQL-like field selection in REST, FIQL/RSQL query DSLs, and governing query complexity limits to prevent abuse.

subskills.name: Bulk & Batch Operation Design Patterns
subskills.description: Designing standards for multi-resource operations — batch request envelopes (JSON Batch, multipart/mixed), partial success handling (HTTP 207 Multi-Status), transactional vs non-transactional batch semantics, and progress tracking for long-running bulk operations.

subskills.name: API Style Guide Authoring & Enforcement
subskills.description: Writing comprehensive API style guides (like Google, Microsoft, Zalando) — naming conventions, mandatory headers, pagination rules, error format, versioning policy — and enforcing compliance via automated linting (Spectral, Optic) in CI/CD pipelines.

subskills.name: Schema Evolution & Compatibility Rules
subskills.description: Defining backward and forward compatibility rules for API schema changes — additive-only field policies, required field introduction strategies, enum extension rules, and automated compatibility checking in CI pipelines.

subskills.name: Hypermedia Controls & Affordance Design
subskills.description: Designing hypermedia affordances — HAL (Hypertext Application Language), JSON:API, Siren, and Ion format evaluation; link relation registries (IANA); and action affordances that guide client state transitions without out-of-band documentation.

junior.description: Models API resources following the organization's domain taxonomy, applies RFC 7807 error response standards consistently, and implements platform-standard pagination conventions for collection endpoints.

mid.description: Evaluates Richardson Maturity levels for API programs, designs query language standards for complex filtering, and architects bulk/batch operation patterns with partial success semantics.
